input: Check if my rental deposit was returned in full

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user may need to check just the amount received, or also investigate deductions, itemised breakdowns, or legal compliance — this defines how deep the task goes.
Knowing whether the deposit was held by a landlord, letting agency, or a government-backed deposit protection scheme changes who to contact and what records to pull.
The country or region determines the legal rules around deposit returns — timelines, required documentation, and dispute resolution processes vary widely.
There are often legal deadlines to raise a dispute after a tenancy ends; knowing how long ago the tenancy ended affects urgency and available options.
Understanding what records the user already has (bank statements, deposit receipts, move-out inspection reports) determines the immediate next action.
The user may just want to confirm the amount, or they may want to dispute deductions and recover money — the definition of 'done' shapes the whole plan.
Some users want to handle this themselves; others want help drafting a formal letter or escalating to a dispute service — preferred approach affects the output.
